title: HTML Document Structure
description: Every HTML document follows a standard structure that helps browsers understand how to display the content correctly.
The structure includes the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration, the <html> element, the <head> section, and the <body> section.
The <head> contains information about the webpage such as the title, while the <body> contains all the visible content that users see.
Understanding this structure is important because it serves as the framework of every HTML webpage.

example.output: A webpage with the title 'My Portfolio' and a heading that says 'Kley's Portfolio'.
